new_statements.quote: Stress in Namia is predictable, occurring on the penultimate syllable of a word. [...] Stress occurs on the penultimate syllable of inflected words, other than verbs. [...] If the final syllable of a word has a heavy core [VV] or [VC], then the stress shifts to that syllable. [...] If the third syllable is a light core (only V with no onset), the stress moves back to the antepenultimate syllable. [...] 4.2 Stress rule exception The one class of words that is stressed differently is the ordinal numbers. On the two syllable number words, the stress is on the last syllable. [...] They are more commonly found in a longer form, and then the stress is penultimate.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and predictable: default on the penultimate syllable (e.g. ['ol.ki] 'heavy', [pla'ko.lu] 'young man'), but a heavy final syllable (vowel sequence VV or closed VC) attracts stress to the final syllable ([i'pir] 'hot', [ka'pou] 'large', [a.nan.ki'ao] 'excellent'); if the (final) third syllable is an onsetless bare V, stress retracts to the antepenult (['no.wi.ə] 'another'). Verbs: penult on verbs of <=3 syllables with only a realis suffix, final if heavy; 4+-syllable verbs with realis suffix take antepenult; adding any prefix to a 2-3 syllable verb moves stress penult->antepenult; a disyllabic suffix puts stress on the suffix's first syllable (word penult), a monosyllabic suffix leaves stress unchanged.
new_statements.exceptions: Two-syllable numerals ('one'...'five') are stressed on the last syllable (sec. 4.2); in their longer forms stress is again penultimate. Verb prefixation/suffixation conditions in sec. 4.1.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the (inflected) word; examples are citation forms with morpheme breaks marked; stress marked with ' before the stressed syllable. Authors state stress is predictable (non-phonemic).
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Namia as a whole (informants from Yaru, Yegarapi and Norambalip villages, Edwaki area, Lumi Sub-District); authors state 'language differences are minimal' across the four social areas. Same language as glottocode nami1256 / ISO nnm; no separate dialect glottocode needed.

sources.note: Sec. 4 'Stress in Namia' pp.16-18: stress predictable, penultimate by default; shifts to final syllable if final has heavy core (VV or VC); moves to antepenult if third syllable is onsetless V; verb-specific rules (4+ syllable verbs with realis suffix -> antepenult; prefixes shift penult->antepenult on 2-3 syll verbs; disyllabic suffix draws stress to penult); exception: two-syllable numerals stressed on last syllable (sec. 4.2).
